doc.title: Frank Foster and Bill Hughes interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Schenectady, New York, March 28, 1995

title: Foster's sneakers solo in England
summary: Foster, late and lacking dress shoes, plays in sneakers until Charlie Fowlkes pulls away his stand.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: My punctuality habits were horrible in those days. So I’d come in late and he would call either “Little Pony” or “Jumpin’ at the Woodside” and I’d have to rise to the occasion immediately. And if something happened, my reed is too dry and I might squeak during the performance, Basie would be the first one to break up and fall off the stool laughing. And the almost embarrassing, most embarrassing thing that ever happened to me was in Manchester, it was either in Manchester or Birmingham, England, I can’t remember which—
Yeah, I was going to bring that up.

I lost my dress shoes. We had a brown and tan tux, and I lost my brown dress shoes. Misplaced them, they weren’t lost, maybe Barracuda got them or something. But anyway, by concert time, I had no dress shoes. And with this brown and tan tuxedo, I had some blue and white sneakers. So it came time for me to take a solo, a big solo. On short solos, one might stand up in front of one’s stand and just play eight measures and sit down. But on long, extended solos, you always came out to the microphone. Well with these blue and white sneakers on, and this brown and tan tuxedo, I didn’t want to come out to the microphone, so I tried to, I stood up at my stand and played my solo. And Charlie Fowlkes, the baritone saxophone, wouldn’t have none of this, so he cooly, very cooly just pulled my bandstand out from in front of me, and thousands of people saw the fellow playing the tenor solo with brown and tan tuxedo and blue and white sneakers, and everybody in the band broke up, the audience broke up, and Basie did his usual falling off the stool.
